chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), regarding
a man who bequeathed his wealth in the Way of Allah. He (peace be upon him) said: Give it to the one to whom he bequeathed it, even if he was a Jew or a Christian.
Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'So whoever alters it after he has heard it, the sin of it is only upon those who alter it.'

key_terms.سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ: Way of Allah (a general category for charity/bequest)

ai.seo_question: Who inherits a bequest made in the Way of Allah if a specific person is named?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a bequest designated for 'sabilillah' is fulfilled by giving the specified amount to the named individual, irrespective of their faith, as the term refers to the recipient rather than a specific cause. It cites Quran 2:181 to emphasize that the testator's intent is binding and should not be altered, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that 'sabilillah' in this context allows for personal beneficiaries. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Islamic inheritance law in accommodating diverse religious communities within the Muslim polity.
